id_naples_crag.blurb: A small crag on the highland flats above the town of Naples in Boundary County, North Idaho, beneath the peak called Roman Nose. Fifteen climbs, mostly short and bouldery, with trad leads making up the bulk and a handful of bolted lines mixed in. Difficulty runs from easy fifth class through the 5.12 range, with the 5.10s being the largest group. The wall looks west, so it warms up in the late afternoon even though trees crowd the base. Many lines can be top-roped by walking around either end of the cliff. A quiet, low-key spot rather than a crowded one.

id_elephant_rock_east.blurb: The east side of Elephant Rock in City of Rocks, one of the busiest faces on the formation. Fifteen climbs, mostly trad with a few bolted lines and one top-rope, on cracks, faces and low-angle slabs. Grades start around 5.7 and climb to the 5.11 range, with the 5.10s the biggest group and a handful of easier lines for moderate leaders. The face looks east, giving morning sun and afternoon shade, which suits warm days. Because the lot sits right below the rock there is almost no walk, so it works well for short days and mixed-ability parties.
id_elephant_rock_east.parking_note: Drive north on Emery Canyon Road to the signed Elephant Rock parking area; the cliff is right beside it.
id_elephant_rock_east.approach: Essentially no approach: a short trail from the parking area leads straight to the base.

id_flaming_rock.blurb: A compact formation in City of Rocks, reached on a sage-lined trail. The steep west face is mostly bolted clip-ups through pockets in rust-orange patina, while the east face is lower in angle and slabbier. Fifteen climbs in all: nine sport, five trad and one top-rope. Grades spread from the 5.7 range through the 5.10s and 5.11s, topping out in the 5.12 range, so there is a short easy line for beginners and steeper tests for stronger climbers. Water runs in a creek on the north side much of the year.

id_jet_a_sector.blurb: The first and shortest of the three sectors on the Discovery Wall, the tallest wall at the Fins, a limestone sport area at the south end of the Lost River Range near Arco. All fifteen routes here are bolted and hard: mostly 5.12 and 5.13 with a few at 5.11, so this is not the place for newer leaders. The limestone is vertical to slightly overhanging with positive edges and pockets. The Fins walls take morning sun and fall into shade by early afternoon, which makes the later part of a hot day workable.
